abstract: Neural network-based virtual microphone estimation (neural-VME) synthesizes microphone signals at unobserved spatial locations from a limited set of real microphone (RM) physical recordings. This enables high-resolution arrays that improve spatial processing for downstream tasks such as speech enhancement. However, existing methods rely on supervised training with ground-truth signals captured at virtual locations, requiring datasets that scale with the number of virtual microphones (VM) and leaving open the question of how to design optimal large-array configurations. We propose Virtual-Flow, a flow-matching framework that implicitly generates VM signals conditioned on real recordings, without requiring ground-truth VM signals. We introduce a semi-supervised training strategy based on pseudo-VM targets constructed from time-delayed superpositions of real recordings. Virtual-Flow shows improved magnitude estimation in high-frequency bands, yielding richer spatial cues for beamforming. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed Virtual-Flow, combined with reflow distillation, outperforms existing neural-VME baselines in VM-based beamforming and achieves competitive end-to-end speech enhancement performance with low computational cost.

oneSentenceThesis: 本文用流匹配从 4 路真麦克风信号生成 12 路虚拟麦克风信号，以时延叠加构造的伪目标加波束形成目标做半监督训练，在 4+12 通道下把波束形成增强从 5.7 dB 提升到 10.3 dB，单步推理仅用 7.8 G MAC/s。
originalTitle: Virtual-Flow: Virtual Microphone-based Speech Enhancement via Semi-supervised Flow Matching
readerTitle: 只用四个真麦克风，怎么“变出” 十二个虚拟麦克风来做增强
